claim_verbatim: Mobile phone reminder trials in Malaysia: SMS + call reminders improved adherence from 54.6% to 92.2% and reduced missed appointments from 35.5% to 14.0% — demonstrating that the structural gap is addressable by systematic outreach, not patient-level attitude change (23)
flag_reason: Single RCT; no independent corroboration of effect-size range

new_sources.title: Mobile Telephone Text Messaging for Medication Adherence in Chronic Disease: A Meta-analysis
new_sources.key_data: SMS text messaging significantly improved medication adherence: OR 2.11 (95% CI 1.52–2.93; p<0.001). Translates to adherence improving from 50% to 67.8% (absolute +17.8%). After study-quality sensitivity adjustment: OR 1.67 (95% CI 1.21–2.29).
new_sources.verbatim_quote: text messaging significantly improved medication adherence (odds ratio, 2.11; 95% CI, 1.52-2.93; P < .001)

new_sources.title: Mobile phone messaging reminders for attendance at healthcare appointments
new_sources.key_data: SMS reminders vs no reminders: RR 1.14 (95% CI 1.03–1.26). Attendance 78.6% (SMS) vs 67.8% (no reminder). SMS cost 55–65% lower than phone call reminders per attendance event.
new_sources.verbatim_quote: Risk ratio of 1.14 (95% CI 1.03 to 1.26) ... attendance rate with text reminders: 78.6% ... attendance rate with no reminders: 67.8%

new_sources.title: What is the effect of mobile phone text message reminders on medication adherence among adult type 2 diabetes mellitus patients: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
new_sources.key_data: T2DM-specific: pooled SMD 0.36 (95% CI 0.14–0.59) for SMS reminders vs usual care on medication adherence. Moderate-certainty GRADE evidence. Includes Adikusuma 2017 (Indonesia) and one Indian RCT.
new_sources.verbatim_quote: The pooled estimated impact of mobile phone text message reminders on medication adherence was (SMD: 0.36; 95%CI; 0.14, 0.59) compared to usual care groups

new_sources.title: The Effect of Education through Short Message Service (SMS) Messages on Diabetic Patients Adherence
new_sources.key_data: Daily SMS education messages for T2DM patients in Indonesia. Significant improvement in MMAS medication adherence score in intervention group (p<0.001) vs control (p=0.019). Between-group difference significant (p<0.05). Positive glycemic trend not statistically significant.
new_sources.verbatim_quote: The provision of education through SMS had a positive effect on medication adherence and glycemic levels. significant differences in MMAS score between the control and intervention groups (p < 0.05)
new_sources.effect_size_label: positive (MMAS score improvement; no absolute % reported)

effect_size_range_summary.low_estimate: Cochrane CD007458: attendance RR 1.14 (67.8%→78.6%, +10.8 pp absolute)
effect_size_range_summary.mid_estimate: JAMA Int Med 2016 meta-analysis (16 RCTs, n=2742): adherence OR 2.11, 50%→67.8% (+17.8 pp). BMC 2023 T2DM-specific: SMD 0.36.
effect_size_range_summary.high_estimate: PMC5433794 (original single Malaysian RCT): 54.6%→92.2% (+37.6 pp) — high end, specific to recall context with combined SMS+phone intervention
effect_size_range_summary.note: The original PMC5433794 figure (54.6%→92.2%) is consistent with the high-end of the literature range. Multi-modal (SMS+call) interventions show stronger effects than SMS-alone. The range across independent meta-analyses is +10–18 pp absolute for SMS-only interventions on adherence/attendance, consistent with the direction of the original claim. The original claim's figure is not refuted but represents an optimistic single-study result; the body of evidence supports the directional claim with a conservative floor of +10 pp.

suggested_revision: Replace single-RCT citation with: 'SMS/digital reminders consistently improve CDM appointment attendance and medication adherence across independent meta-analyses: Cochrane review (8 RCTs, n=6,615) finds attendance increases from 67.8% to 78.6% with SMS (RR 1.14; 95% CI 1.03–1.26) (Gurol-Urganci 2013); JAMA Internal Medicine meta-analysis (16 RCTs, n=2,742) finds SMS approximately doubles odds of medication adherence (OR 2.11; 50%→67.8%) (Thakkar 2016); T2DM-specific meta-analysis (9 RCTs, n=1,121) confirms SMD 0.36 (moderate GRADE) (BMC 2023); and an Indonesian RCT confirms significant MMAS adherence improvement with SMS education in T2DM patients (Adikusuma 2017). Malaysian single-clinic RCT showing 54.6%→92.2% adherence with combined SMS+phone intervention (PMC5433794) reflects the high-end of the literature range consistent with multi-modal outreach.'
reasoning: Four independent peer-reviewed sources (one Cochrane review, two meta-analyses, one Indonesia-specific RCT) corroborate the directional claim that SMS/digital reminders significantly improve CDM attendance and medication adherence. The effect-size range across sources is consistent, with the original Malaysian figure being at the high end but not contradicted. The claim now has multi-source academic backing.
